titleStmt.title: Telegram From the Embassy in Paraguay to the Department of State

div.head: 401. Telegram From the Embassy in Paraguay to the Department of State
div.p: 2. Summary: While main reason for invitation was supposedly to express gratitude for arrival of five-man flood evaluation team, it became evident that President wanted to express his discontent at present trend of press coverage by “ABC Color” newspaper. Other subjects discussed were record publicity, Laino expulsion, military and economic aid, and, of course, events in Bolivia. End summary.

3. Flood conversation opened by expression of gratitude for our disaster relief funds allocated to Indian colonies along the Paraguay River plus profuse thanks for the fast cooperation in arrival and meetings with the five-man evaluation team. President mentioned great aid to Argentina by Vatican and others while only USA had come to Paraguay’s help thus far. Then stating that Paraguayans were tough and took their bad times and setbacks stoically and without tears as they had through history, the general then launched into a tirade against the negative criticisms of “ABC Color.”

4. “ABC Color” activities. Not only the Colorados have been discussing the consistent anti-government articles by “ABC” but even the general public and some opposition members have privately expressed concern at the frequency and vehemence of some “ABC” articles. Zuccolillo (Owner of “ABC”) has several times expressed concern at prospect of closing and as recently as a month ago Ambassador had expressed to Minister of Interior Montanaro the negative effects on Paraguay that such a closure would have. However, immediately after expressing these concerns two weeks ago, “ABC” carried a Laino interview, which could hurt efforts to get Laino’s return approved and certainly strengthened displeasure of government.

5. President Stroessner first decried the unbalanced
amount of anti-government criticism and seemed especially provoked by report on the ineffectiveness of the legislature and the negative comments on Paraguay’s participation in Itaipu. President stressed that criticism should be made on basis of grounds to improve conditions and not merely as a confrontation between press and government. Seriousness of his concern was the denunciation of Conrado Pappalardo’s sister, who is married to Zuccolillo, apparently to let Ambassador know such association would not affect his decision. He was also provoked that “ABC” did not carry his anti-communist interview of several days ago although a copy was provided to them.

6. Ambassador noted traditional right of free press and value of dialogue to keep all on their toes plus impressing upon Stroessner the vast negative effects of any closure on our mutual personal efforts over last nine months as well as the relations between our two countries.

7. Never could Ambassador extract a promise or statement from President that “ABC” would not be closed but received half-hearted agreement that nothing would happen during Ambassador’s trip to the US.

8. The mention of effecting our relations, brought the question of when we could give more military and economic aid to Paraguay. Ambassador stated the betterment of human rights in Paraguay was a step in the right direction but a newspaper’s closure would cancel any prospects.

9. Aid for Paraguay. President then repeated his previous remarks that we should grant Paraguay at least the same aid as Bolivia and again repeating the comparison of pro-communist and anti-US Bolivia to anti-communist and pro-US Paraguay. The theme “amigos con nuestros amigos” was once again heard.

10. Ricord. Once again Ambassador was requested to compile everything possible on information on the Ricord case, particularly if we have anything on statements by Ricord as to his associates in drug trafficking in Paraguay. President pledged his support and cooperation to counteract the small drug trafficking in Paraguay.

11. Visit by Assistant Secretary Enders. President stated his pleasure at Ambassador Enders’ visit for his “Cambio de Mando” on August 15. (Upon leaving, Conrado Pappalardo also talked about Ambassador Enders’ trip for August 15 and stated he had urged that Mrs. Enders be sure to accompany her husband.)

12. Upon leaving, Ambassador reiterated his concerns over any closure of “ABC” and any prolonged expulsion of Laino and surprisingly, as opposed to Minister Montanaro’s remarks (Asuncion 1582). President stated that plans were being studied for his return.

13. Comments: Several times during conversation Ambassador attempted to interject discussion on opening up the political process in Paraguay and finally was told “lets’s meet on that upon your return.”
14. President Stroessner seems to be in excellent health, more alert and active than nine months ago. He also seems to be watching his weight and getting more rest than previously.

note.p: Source: Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D830238–0557. Confidential.

In telegram 1155 from Asuncion, March 28, the Embassy reported: “The prominent exiled opposition leader Domingo Laino was prevented by the GOP from entering Paraguay. Laino’s return was designed to test the genuineness of the Interior Minister’s claim that exiles would be allowed into Paraguay if they returned one by one. The GOP’s refusal to allow Laino to enter the country has provided the opposition with new ammunition to conduct its public relations sniping of the GOP.” (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D830171–0246)
Memorandum of conversation for this meeting has not been found.
Reference is to Auguste Ricord who was extradited to the United States in 1972. See Foreign Relations, 1969–1976, vol. E–10, Documents on American Republics, 1969–1972, Document 574.

In telegram 1330 from Asuncion, April 7, the Embassy confirmed a “request by GOP officials for luncheon April 13 with Assistant Secretary Enders.” (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D830193–0180) In telegram 1370 from Asuncion, April 11, the Embassy described: “personalities probable topics for Enders-Montanaro/Pappalardo luncheon April 13.” (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D830200–0539) No memorandum of conversation for the meeting has been found.

No indication of an August 15 visit by Enders has been found. In telegram 3369 from Asuncion, August 16, the Embassy reported: “President Alfredo Stroessner was sworn in on August 15 for seventh term as President of Paraguay, capping three days of ceremonies. The general populace appears to have taken the President’s inauguration for another 5-year term as simply a matter of course, and virtually the only event which provided much occasion for comment and speculation was the installation of three new cabinet members.” (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D830471–1013) In telegram 228836 to Asuncion, August 12, the Department instructed the Embassy to deliver a message from Reagan to Stroessner upon his inauguration: “Dear Mr. President: Please accept my congratulations and best wishes as you commence a new presidential term. The American people share my hope that the close friendship between Paraguay and the United States will continue in the years ahead. Sincerely, Ronald Reagan.” (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D830463–0863)

In telegram 1582 from Asuncion, April 26, the Embassy wrote: “In Ambassador Davis’ first meeting with Minister Montanaro since Paraguayan group luncheon with Assistant Secretary Enders, points discussed at this meeting were present condition of human rights in Paraguay and possible Enders visit. Minister Montanaro was very pleased with his treatment in Washington and felt Ambassador Enders had conversed in a friendly and open manner with them. Minister was openly impressed by Ambassador Enders’ knowledge of Paraguay’s problems.” Additionally, the Embassy noted that Stroessner had “called off” Laino’s return and that “it was evident that only the president can made new decision to allow the return should it be requested.” (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D830233–0634)

In telegram 3428 from Asuncion, August 19, the Embassy wrote: “The inauguration August 15 of President Alfredo Stroessner for a seventh term (1983–1988) occurred within the context of (A) discouraging economic and political developments and trends in Paraguay, and (B) a rapidly changing hemispheric and regional environment. The Embassy believes it timely, therefore, to propose a careful review of U.S. interests and objectives in Paraguay in the light of the current context in order to arrive at appropriate and agreed USG policy responses and courses of action.” Furthermore: “I must say I have been quite disappointed that I have not been more successful in my efforts to talk sense to the Stroessner government, to urge it to understand that its own interests lie in better observance of democratic rules. Maybe after about thirty years in office, President Stroessner just is not going to change. It is a pity, because by not loosening up, he is creating a dangerous situation for the future. I don’t think that we can afford to be identified with that wrong approach if we are going to have an influence on the situation later on. Fortunately, a lot of Colorados and even a lot of generals agree with me, or at least they say so.” (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D830505–0170)

In telegram 281942 to Asuncion, October 1, the Department wrote: “Department welcomed Embassy’s review of developments and trends in Paraguay and related recommendations regarding USG policy objectives and agrees that a cautious shift in the balance of our policy objectives toward Paraguay is called for. However, in implementing the above strategy, we want to avoid, whenever possible, jeopardizing GOP cooperation on hemispheric or international issues and/or compromising access to and influence with key Paraguayans on domestic issues such a human rights, democracy and the economy. Periodic evaluation of the effectiveness and impact of this policy adjustment as it is implemented would be helpful to the Department in understanding the situation and tuning our course appropriately.” (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D830571–0025)
